source_caption:
Tulsa King (2022) is a crime drama series starring Sylvester Stallone as Dwight “The General” Manfredi, a New York Mafia capo who is released after 25 years in prison and unexpectedly sent to Tulsa, Oklahoma. After sacrificing decades of his life for his crime family, Dwight quickly realizes that the people he was loyal to no longer have a place for him.

Starting over in a city where he knows almost nobody, Dwight begins building a new circle of allies while trying to establish his influence. But his old-school Mafia mentality constantly clashes with the modern world, forcing him to adapt while dealing with enemies, betrayal, and the consequences of his past.

At its core, Tulsa King explores loyalty, betrayal, family, reinvention, and the struggle to find purpose after losing years of your life. Dwight may be a criminal, but the series also shows his more human side as he tries to reconnect with his family and create something that belongs to him.

More than just a crime series, it’s a story about an aging man getting a second chance to rebuild his life—even when the only world he knows is the one that keeps pulling him back. ❤️‍🩹

💬 Do you think Dwight can truly leave his old life behind and start over? Let us know in the comments! 👇

source_details.synopsis: Tulsa King is an American comedy and crime drama television series created by Taylor Sheridan for the streaming platform Paramount+. The series stars Sylvester Stallone as Dwight "The General" Manfredi, an American Mafia caporegime who has been recently released from prison in New York and is sent to Tulsa, Oklahoma, where he begins to set up a criminal organization. It is Stallone's first leading role in a scripted television series. The series also stars Andrea Savage, Martin Starr, Jay Will, Max Casella, Domenick Lombardozzi, Vincent Piazza, A. C.
